value.name: San Jacinto Power (SJP)
value.notes: CORRECTION (2026-08-10): an earlier session incorrectly recorded this field as SCE-direct, reasoning from Western Community Energy's 2021 dissolution without checking for a separate, single-city CCA. San Jacinto Power is confirmed via its own official site (sanjacintopower.com, linked directly from the City's own site) as a real, currently operating CCA exclusive to San Jacinto, with automatic/default customer enrollment (the site states 'As a San Jacinto Power customer, you have several options,' describing SJP PrimePower as the default rate plan, SJP PureGreen as an opt-up, and an explicit Opt Out page to return to standard SCE service). SCE continues to deliver the power and provide billing/customer service.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes San Jacinto/Riverside County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

value.notes: The City's own page, titled 'Instant Solar Permit,' states the permit is issued 'instantly' for code-compliant systems submitted through SolarAPP+.

other_conditions: Only for use by contractors registered with SolarAPP+
Covers roof-mounted solar photovoltaic panel installations with or without an energy storage system
A main electrical service upgrade can be added to the Instant Solar Permit
Only systems included on the SolarAPP+ Eligibility Checklist lists are eligible
